reading.title: California Pressured By Two Hollywood Unions to Settle Paramount-Warner Bros. Antitrust Lawsuit
reading.text:
At the center of one of the most consequential entertainment law disputes of 2026 is the proposed $111 billion merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery. A coalition of 12 state attorneys general, led by California AG Rob Bonta, filed an antitrust lawsuit to block the deal after the Trump Department of Justice approved it in June 2026. The DOJ's clearance was controversial: AG Bonta publicly argued that 'the Trump administration has absolutely dropped the ball,' alleging the DOJ ignored the advice of its own staff in greenlighting the merger. The states contend the deal would substantially reduce competition in streaming, news, and theatrical distribution, raise consumer prices, reduce programming output, and narrow studio slates.

The antitrust trial has been scheduled for March 2027 — a timeline that has fractured Hollywood's labor community. The Directors Guild of America (DGA) and IATSE sent a joint letter to both AG Bonta and Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison urging them to reach a settlement or, at minimum, expedite the trial. The two unions, which jointly represent nearly 200,000 film and television workers across the U.S. and Canada, argued that the prolonged uncertainty is already causing productions to be put on hold or canceled, further devastating workers in an already depressed market. DGA executive director Russell Hollander and IATSE president Matthew Loeb proposed specific settlement conditions, including that Paramount and Warner Bros. continue operating as entirely separate studios and that the combined company maintain U.S. production levels and keep Paramount headquartered in Los Angeles.

The unions find themselves at odds with the Writers Guild of America, which has been vociferously opposed to the merger and sued to seek a complete block. SAG-AFTRA staked out a middle position, supporting the states' suit but indicating it could accept the deal with 'enforceable safeguards' through a settlement. The Teamsters similarly demanded the deal be blocked unless specific workforce conditions were met.

On the legal offensive, Paramount filed a motion demanding that the state AG plaintiffs post a $1,884,726,092 bond — approximately $1.88 billion — to cover damages if the states lose the case. Paramount argued this is required under the Clayton Act and other federal law, noting the company faces roughly $7 million per day in fees owed to WBD shareholders under the merger agreement. Meanwhile, Paramount has secured antitrust clearance from 68 countries globally, leaving the multi-state U.S. lawsuit as the sole remaining legal obstacle to completing the deal.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 反垄断许可，指监管机构审查并批准某项合并或收购不会违反竞争法的正式许可文件。
vocabulary.example: The acquiring company obtained antitrust clearance from regulators in 68 jurisdictions before the domestic challenge stalled the transaction.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 各州总检察长（复数形式），是州政府的最高法律官员，有权代表州提起诉讼，包括反垄断诉讼。
vocabulary.example: A coalition of attorneys general from multiple states coordinated their legal strategy before filing the joint complaint in federal court.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 《克莱顿法》，美国联邦反垄断成文法之一，规范可能实质性削减竞争的合并行为，并授权当事方申请损害赔偿保证金。
vocabulary.example: Paramount invoked the Clayton Act in its motion, arguing that the state plaintiffs were required to post a substantial bond before the injunction could be maintained.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 可强制执行的保护条款，指并入合并协议或和解令中、具有法律约束力并可诉诸法院执行的条件或限制措施。
vocabulary.example: SAG-AFTRA indicated it could support the merger only if the final consent decree included enforceable safeguards protecting minimum domestic production quotas.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 合并协议，规定两家公司合并条款的正式合同，通常包含终止费、股东补偿及违约条款等关键条款。
vocabulary.example: Under the terms of the merger agreement, Paramount was obligated to pay WBD shareholders approximately $7 million per day until the transaction either closed or was formally abandoned.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 原告缴纳保证金，指法院要求申请禁令的诉讼方预先存入一定金额，若其败诉则用于赔偿被告因禁令而遭受的损失。
vocabulary.example: The defendant corporation moved to require the plaintiffs post a bond of nearly two billion dollars, arguing that the injunctive relief sought would cost the company millions daily.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 和解条件，指当事方在诉讼外解决争议时须满足的具体要求，通常以行为承诺或结构性补救措施形式呈现。
vocabulary.example: The unions proposed settlement conditions requiring the merged entity to maintain separate operational structures and preserve existing headcount at both studios.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 院线发行，指通过电影院向公众放映影片的商业渠道，是反垄断审查中评估市场集中度的关键相关市场之一。
vocabulary.example: The states argued that consolidation of theatrical distribution among fewer major studios would reduce output diversity and enable coordinated pricing at the exhibition level.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 实质性削减竞争，美国反垄断法核心审查标准，指某项交易在特定相关市场中将显著限制有效竞争，构成违法合并的法定门槛。
vocabulary.example: The state plaintiffs argued that combining the two largest legacy studios would substantially reduce competition in both premium scripted programming and live news broadcasting.

vocabulary.definition_cn: 反垄断诉讼，依据《谢尔曼法》《克莱顿法》等反垄断成文法提起的诉讼，旨在阻止或救济损害市场竞争的商业行为或合并交易。
vocabulary.example: Filing an antitrust lawsuit to block a merger cleared by the federal DOJ is procedurally unusual but legally permissible under the doctrine of state enforcement standing.

sentence_patterns.pattern: [Coalition of parties] filed an antitrust lawsuit to block [transaction], contending that the deal would substantially reduce competition in [relevant markets] and [harm].
sentence_patterns.example: A coalition of 12 state attorneys general filed an antitrust lawsuit to block the merger, contending that the deal would substantially reduce competition in streaming, news, and theatrical distribution and raise consumer prices.
sentence_patterns.translation_cn: 由12位州总检察长组成的联盟提起反垄断诉讼，要求阻止该合并交易，主张该交易将实质性削减流媒体、新闻及院线发行领域的竞争，并推高消费者价格。

sentence_patterns.pattern: [Party] filed a motion demanding that [opposing party] post a [amount] bond to cover damages in the event [adverse outcome].
sentence_patterns.example: Paramount filed a motion demanding that the state AG plaintiffs post a $1,884,726,092 bond to cover damages if the states lose the case.
sentence_patterns.translation_cn: 派拉蒙提出动议，要求各州总检察长原告缴纳约18.85亿美元保证金，以备各州败诉时承担赔偿责任。

sentence_patterns.pattern: [Party] proposed specific settlement conditions, including that [structural remedy] and that [behavioral remedy].
sentence_patterns.example: The unions proposed specific settlement conditions, including that Paramount and Warner Bros. continue operating as entirely separate studios and that the combined company maintain U.S. production levels.
sentence_patterns.translation_cn: 工会提出具体和解条件，要求派拉蒙与华纳兄弟继续作为完全独立的制片公司运营，且合并后的公司须维持美国本土制作规模。

summary_cn: 2026年，派拉蒙与华纳兄弟迪斯科维合并案引发多州反垄断诉讼。加州总检察长领衔12州联盟起诉阻止该1110亿美元交易，指其实质性削减市场竞争。美国导演工会与IATSE致函呼吁和解或加速审判，以保障近20万影视工人就业。派拉蒙则要求原告缴纳约18.85亿美元保证金，该案已成2026年娱乐法领域最具影响力的诉讼之一。
legal_analysis:
① 核心法律问题：本案核心在于州政府是否有权在联邦司法部已批准合并后，依据《克莱顿法》独立提起诉讼阻止该交易，以及合并是否构成对流媒体、新闻及院线发行相关市场的实质性反竞争损害。

② 美国法律框架分析：《谢尔曼法》与《克莱顿法》共同构成美国联邦反垄断法的基础框架，但各州总检察长亦享有依据《哈特-斯科特-罗迪诺法》及州反垄断法独立执法的诉讼资格。联邦司法部批准不能剥夺州的起诉权，这一"双轨执法"机制是本案程序上最值得关注之处。此外，派拉蒙要求原告缴纳保证金的动议依据《克莱顿法》第16条，旨在以财务压力迫使州政府放弃诉讼——这一策略在大型并购阻击诉讼中日益常见。工会分裂立场则揭示了劳工利益与竞争政策之间的内在张力。

③ 对中国娱乐法律师的实践启示：中国律师参与跨国并购审查时，须高度关注美国州级反垄断执法的独立性；在设计合并协议时，应将多辖区监管风险、终止费条款及保证金义务纳入尽职调查范围，同时评估劳工组织在并购监管博弈中的实质性法律影响力。
cn_us_comparison: 美国反垄断执法呈现联邦与州两级并行的双轨制结构：联邦司法部依据《克莱顿法》审查合并，各州总检察长亦可独立提起诉讼，两者结论可以相悖，如本案所示。中国则实行单一集中的反垄断执法体制：依据2022年修订的《反垄断法》及《经营者集中审查办法》，国家市场监督管理总局（市监总局）是唯一具有合并审查权的主管机关，不存在省级执法机构独立起诉的机制。在救济手段上，美国法院可命令原告缴纳损害赔偿保证金，中国法律框架中尚无类似制度安排。此外，美国工会在反垄断诉讼中享有较强的参与和施压空间，而中国《工会法》赋予工会的功能主要集中于劳动关系协调，在并购监管层面的法律介入渠道较为有限。两国制度差异对跨国并购的合规策略设计具有重要参考价值。
discussion_prompt: Given that Paramount has already secured antitrust clearance from 68 countries and the Trump DOJ approved the merger, should state attorneys general retain the legal standing to unilaterally block a transaction of national economic significance — and does this dual-enforcement architecture ultimately serve or undermine the coherent development of U.S. competition policy?

writing_exercise.prompt: You are a legal analyst drafting a client memo. In 2-3 sentences, describe a hypothetical scenario in which a coalition of state regulators files an antitrust lawsuit to block a proposed merger, proposes specific settlement conditions, and demands that the opposing party post a substantial bond.
writing_exercise.model_answer: A coalition of nine state attorneys general filed an antitrust lawsuit to block the proposed $85 billion acquisition of a major sports broadcaster, contending that the deal would substantially reduce competition in live sports rights markets and harm consumers through coordinated price increases. The states proposed specific settlement conditions, including that the target continue operating its regional sports networks as structurally independent entities and that the acquirer maintain domestic broadcast employment levels for a minimum of five years. In response, the acquiring company filed a motion demanding that the state AG plaintiffs post a $1.2 billion bond under the Clayton Act, arguing that the injunctive delay was costing shareholders approximately $4 million per day under the terms of the merger agreement.

youtube_rec.title: State AG Antitrust Power: Can States Block a Merger the DOJ Approved? | Paramount-WBD Explained
youtube_rec.summary_cn: 本视频深入解析美国联邦与州反垄断执法双轨制的运作机制，以派拉蒙与华纳兄弟迪斯科维合并案为核心案例，探讨州总检察长在联邦司法部已批准并购后独立提起诉讼的法律依据、《克莱顿法》保证金制度及相关政策争议，适合希望理解美国竞争法执法结构的法律从业者。

extended_reading.description_cn: Norton Rose Fulbright梳理2026年六大AI版权诉讼案（含Bartz v. Anthropic、Disney v. Midjourney），分析AI训练使用版权作品是否构成合理使用，以及授权协议作为行业解决路径的兴起趋势。

extended_reading.title: The AI Input Class: Constitutional Urgency and Fair Licensing in AI Copyright Class Actions
extended_reading.description_cn: 纽约大学知识产权与娱乐法学刊学术论文，主张AI版权集体诉讼具有宪法层面的紧迫性，任何授权制度须切实保护人类创作者的核心角色，而非仅提供象征性补偿。
